title: H1 Essay Questions by Topic
doc: 2c H1 Essay Questions by Topic v0.14.docx

sections.title: 1. What this doc is and how it was built
bullets: All H1 Section C essay questions (Q4–Q6, 13 marks each): 123 questions from 41 school-years (117 pages). No essay uses a diagram.

Grouped under Cluster 1 by syllabus sub-topic, then by school and year: 1.1.1 SUD (7), 1.1.2 Sustainable Cities (29), 1.1.3 Liveable Cities (34), 1.2.1 Science of CC (9), 1.2.2 Effects of CC (11), 1.2.3 Responses to CC (33).
Under each question heading, a 'Syllabus' line gives the key question it tests (as in doc 1).

Question wording is typed from each school's question paper. Every essay was checked: 13 marks, and the wording matches the verbatim wording in the reading notes (all 123 match; the only differences are abbreviations in the notes).
Changes in v0.14: each school's essay starts on a new page. Where one school set two essays on the same sub-topic, they share a page (6 cases).

sections.title: 2. Assumptions
bullets: An essay is filed under the sub-topic of its key question. Nine essays have two key questions; they are filed under the first (see section 3 for those that span two sub-topics).
Within a sub-topic, essays are listed by school and year, not by key question (see section 4).
Word files were converted to PDF with LibreOffice before extracting text, so line breaks can differ slightly from the printed paper.
The section line is standardised to 'Section C — Cluster 1: Sustainable Future and Climate Change'.
VJC 2026 is left out (password-protected question paper). MI 2026, NJC 2024 and RVHS 2024–2026 have no H1 paper.
Each school's question starts on a new page for printing; a topic heading stays on the page of its first question.

sections.title: 3. To review: essays that span two sub-topics
sections.note: Each is filed under the first key question. Say if you would rather file it under the second.

sections.title: 4. To consider
bullets: List essays within each sub-topic by key question instead of by school (e.g. all 'women in the city' essays together under 1.1.3). This makes it easy to compare how different schools phrase the same question.
Add a one-page index: key question → schools and years that set an essay on it.
Fit more on a page (e.g. a table with one row per essay) for a quick-revision version.
